tip: Putting several pictures on top of each other to make one picture.
meaning: Compositing stacks layers. A person filmed in front of a green screen, a drawing of a forest and a title can become one scene.
example: A weather reporter in front of a moving map.
vukem: Stacked tracks are composited, and the preview and the export use the same render plan. See [Render](/docs/concepts/render).

tip: How solid something is: 100% is solid, 0% is invisible.
meaning: Lower the opacity and the layer becomes see-through, so what is under it shows.
example: A watermark set to 30% so it does not hide the video.
vukem: `opacity` is a property of an item and can be keyframed, from 0 to 1.

tip: Information stored with a picture that says which parts are see-through.
meaning: Besides red, green and blue, some images keep a fourth value, alpha, for each pixel: 0 is invisible, 1 is solid. A logo with a transparent background has an alpha channel.
example: A PNG logo with no white box around it.

tip: A rule for how a layer mixes with the layers under it.
meaning: Normal just covers what is below. Other modes add, multiply or lighten the colours, to make glows, shadows and light leaks.
example: A sparkle video on a black background looks good when its blend mode is Screen: the black disappears.
vukem: `clip.set_blend`: normal, multiply, screen, overlay or add. See [Effects and color](/docs/guide/effects-and-color).

tip: A blend mode that makes the picture darker, where black stays black and white disappears.
meaning: Multiply mixes the colours of the layer with those below and always gives a darker result. White does nothing.
example: A paper texture on top of a video makes it look printed.

tip: A blend mode that makes the picture lighter, where black disappears.
meaning: Screen is the opposite of multiply and always makes things lighter. Black does nothing.
example: Fire or sparkles filmed on black are placed on a scene with Screen.

tip: A blend mode that makes dark parts darker and bright parts brighter, adding contrast.
meaning: Overlay combines multiply and screen, so it increases contrast and keeps the lightest and the darkest points.
example: A texture that gives a picture more punch.

tip: Anything added on top of a video, like a logo, a title or a sticker.
meaning: In editing, an overlay is an extra layer drawn over the main video.
example: A channel logo in the corner of the screen.

tip: A shape that decides which part of a layer is visible.
meaning: A mask hides everything outside its shape. You can use it to show a video through a circle, or to hide an unwanted thing.
example: Showing a face inside a round bubble.
vukem: `clip.set_mask` limits an item to a rectangle or an ellipse, with a soft edge and an invert option.

tip: Making the edge of a mask soft instead of sharp.
meaning: A feathered edge fades slowly from visible to hidden, so the shape blends in smoothly.
example: A round spotlight with a soft border.

tip: A picture that tells which parts of another picture to keep.
meaning: A matte is black where you hide and white where you show. It is a mask saved as an image, or a clip.
example: A black and white drawing of a bird used to cut a bird shape out of a video.

tip: Removing one colour, usually green or blue, to put something else behind.
meaning: You film a person in front of a plain green wall. The editor makes every green pixel see-through, so you can place any background behind.
example: A kid sits in front of green cloth and the video puts them on the Moon.
vukem: `clip.set_chroma_key` sets the colour, the similarity, the smoothness and the spill. See [Effects and color](/docs/guide/effects-and-color).

tip: Green light bouncing from the screen onto the person, giving a green edge.
meaning: Light from a green screen reflects on hair and shoulders. After keying, a green fringe remains, and spill removal takes the green out of it.
example: A green glow around someone's hair.

tip: A moment where you set a value; the program fills in everything between two keyframes.
meaning: Instead of drawing every frame, you say: at second 1 the box is here, at second 3 it is there. The computer works out the movement between.
example: A star that starts small at 0 seconds and ends big at 2 seconds.
vukem: `keyframe.set` for x, y, scale, rotation, opacity and volume. See [Animate with keyframes](/docs/guide/keyframes).

tip: The in-between pictures computed between two keyframes.
meaning: "Tween" is short for in-between. Artists draw the key poses and tweening fills the rest.
example: A ball keyframed at the top and at the bottom: the falling is the tween.

tip: Making things move by changing them from one frame to the next.
meaning: In editing, animation means changing position, size, turn or see-through-ness over time.
example: A title slides in, stays, and slides out.

tip: Moving, resizing or turning a layer.
meaning: Transform changes where a layer is (position), how big (scale) and how rotated.
example: Make a logo smaller and put it in the corner.
vukem: `item.set_transform` sets x, y, scale, rotation and opacity.

tip: The spot a layer turns and scales around.
meaning: A layer rotates around its anchor point like a door around its hinge. Move the anchor and the same turn looks different.
example: A clock hand turns around its centre, its anchor.

tip: Cutting off the edges of a picture.
meaning: Cropping removes the sides, the top or the bottom, to hide something or change the shape.
example: Crop a wide video so a person fills a tall frame.
vukem: `clip.set_framing` has a crop for each side. See [Clip properties](/docs/guide/clip-properties).

tip: How a picture is placed inside the frame: filling it, or fitting inside.
meaning: Cover fills the whole frame and cuts what does not fit. Contain shows all of the picture and leaves empty bars. None keeps the original size.
example: A wide video in a tall frame: cover cuts the sides; contain shows black bars above and below.

tip: Making a picture soft and out of focus on purpose.
meaning: Blur hides detail. Editors use it to hide faces or car plates, or to make a background soft.
example: A blurred copy of the video fills the empty bars of a vertical video.

tip: The smear of something that moves fast while the camera is open.
meaning: When an object moves during the time the camera takes a frame, it leaves a streak. It makes movement look smooth and real.
example: A spinning fan blade looks like a soft circle.

tip: A quick effect that changes how the whole picture looks.
meaning: A filter changes colours or details in one step, like making it black and white or warm.
example: A sepia filter on an old family video.
vukem: `clip.set_filter`: grayscale, sepia, invert, warm or cool, with an amount.

tip: Anything that changes how a clip looks or sounds.
meaning: Blur, glow, a colour change, an echo: effects change a clip without changing the original file.
example: A zoom pulse on every beat.

tip: Visual effects: pictures made or changed after filming.
meaning: VFX is the work that adds what the camera could not film: explosions, creatures, removed wires.
example: A dragon flying over a real village.

tip: Computer-generated images: pictures made by a computer, not a camera.
meaning: CGI means 3D models and animation created in software, then placed into a video.
example: A talking animal in a family film.

tip: Animated shapes, text and icons, rather than filmed footage.
meaning: Motion graphics are moving designs: titles that fly, charts that grow, shapes that bounce.
example: An animated bar chart in a news video.
vukem: `shape.add` creates rectangles, rounded rectangles and ellipses to animate. See [Shapes](/docs/guide/shapes).

tip: A small video shown over a bigger one.
meaning: Picture-in-picture puts a small window on top of the main video. It is used for reactions and tutorials.
example: A gamer's face in the corner of the game footage.

tip: Showing two or more videos side by side at the same time.
meaning: The frame is divided into parts and each shows a different video.
example: Two friends on a phone call, shown side by side.

tip: Following a moving point in a video, so something else can follow it.
meaning: A tracker finds a spot in every frame. You can then attach text or a blur that stays on that spot as it moves.
example: A name tag that follows a player across the field.

tip: Tracing around something frame by frame to cut it out.
meaning: Rotoscoping draws the outline of a person or an object on every frame. It is slow work, used when no green screen exists.
example: Cutting a person out of a normal video so the background can change.

tip: Which layer is in front of which.
meaning: Layers are drawn from bottom to top. The one on top covers the others unless it is see-through.
example: The caption is placed above the video, so you see it.
vukem: The preview and the export draw the tracks from the bottom row up, so the track at the top of the timeline is drawn on top.
